title: A Cmd.define handler's ctx is never when the machine ctx is undefined
rawReport:
## Summary
A `Cmd.define`d handler's ctx is typed `never` when the machine's `Ctx` is `undefined`, so `ok` / `err` cannot be called from it without widening the handler's `Ctx` by hand.

## What I was doing
Building #282 (epic #273): rewriting `docs/how-to/hand-wire-a-resilient-call.md` so the reader's machine uses `ctx: undefined` and a hand-written `resilient_run` handler that returns `ok(...)` / `err(...)`.

## What I observed
`Interpret<UserMsg, UserCmd, undefined>` made `ok` and `err` "not callable" (TS2349). `InterpretCell` types a defined Cmd's ctx as `Ctx & PortEmitter & OutcomeHelpers<…>` (`src/pure/core.ts`), and `undefined & {…}` reduces to `never`. The page works around it by typing the table `Interpret<UserMsg, UserCmd, unknown>`. Several ported tests typed handlers `as never` for the same reason.

## Why it matters
`ctx: undefined` is the common shape in the docs and tests. Every reader who hand-writes an outcome handler for such a machine hits a confusing type error on the very helpers ADR 0021 hands them.

## Pointers
- `src/pure/core.ts` — `InterpretCell`, the `Ctx & PortEmitter & OutcomeHelpers` intersection
- `src/docs/how-to/hand-wire-resilient-call.test.ts` — the `unknown` workaround
- Epic #273, child #282

## Suggested next step (non-binding)
Type the ctx half as `(Ctx extends undefined ? unknown : Ctx) & PortEmitter & OutcomeHelpers<…>` (or treat `undefined` / `void` like `unknown`) and add a `test-d` case for a machine with `ctx: undefined`.

enriched:
## Summary

When a machine's `Ctx` is `undefined`, a handler's `ctx` type collapses to `never`. For a `Cmd.define`d Cmd that means `ctx.ok` / `ctx.err` (ADR 0021) cannot be called (TS2349). Readers who write a handler for a `ctx: undefined` machine, which is the common shape in `docs/`, hit a confusing type error.

## Cause (read at `origin/main`)

`InterpretCell` in `src/pure/core.ts` types the handler ctx as an intersection:

- a `Cmd.define`d cell: `Ctx & PortEmitter & OutcomeHelpers<OkOfCmd<C>, DeclaredErrorsOf<C>>`
- a hand-written cell: `Ctx & PortEmitter`

With `Ctx = undefined`, `undefined & {…}` reduces to `never`. Triage note: the hand-written arm breaks the same way (`ctx.emit` is unreachable). `InterpretDetached` in the same file has the same `Ctx & PortEmitter` shape. Fix every arm with one shared helper rather than patching each one separately.

Current workarounds on main: `src/docs/how-to/hand-wire-resilient-call.test.ts` types its table `Interpret<UserMsg, UserCmd, unknown>`, and some ported tests cast handlers `as never`.

## Fix direction

Map an `undefined` / `void` Ctx to a neutral base before the intersection, e.g. `(Ctx extends undefined ? unknown : Ctx) & PortEmitter & …` behind one named helper type. This is what the filer suggested, and nothing in the repo contradicts it. `NoCtx` (the named "reads nothing" ctx) already works because it is an object type.

Triage note: searched open issues for an owner of this surface (handler ctx typing); nothing absorbs it. #298 is a different bug (a handler dispatching its own `_ok` Msg).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `Cmd.define`d handler in `Interpret<M, C, undefined>` can call `ctx.ok(...)` and `ctx.err(...)` without a cast, and a hand-written handler in the same table can call `ctx.emit(...)`
- [ ] The same holds for `InterpretDetached` with `Ctx = undefined`
- [ ] A `*.test-d.ts` case under `src/__tests__/` covers a `ctx: undefined` machine with a `Cmd.define`d handler, and includes an `@ts-expect-error` that proves `err` still rejects an undeclared tag
- [ ] `src/docs/how-to/hand-wire-resilient-call.test.ts` and `docs/how-to/hand-wire-a-resilient-call.md` type the table with the machine's real `Ctx` (`undefined`) rather than `unknown`
- [ ] The `as never` handler casts that existed only to work around this are removed
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` pass, and `docs/reference/` is regenerated if the public type changed
